title: The Traveller and His Dog
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Traveller was about to start on a journey, and said to his Dog, who was stretching himself by the door, "Come, what are you yawning for? Hurry up and get ready: I mean you to go with me." But the Dog merely wagged his tail and said quietly, "I'm ready, master: it's you I'm waiting for."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what was the Traveller about to do?
According to the passage, what was the Dog doing when the Traveller spoke to him?
According to the passage, what does the Traveller ask the Dog about?
According to the passage, what does the Traveller tell the Dog to do?
options: Stay behind and guard the house
Hurry up and get ready to go with him
Wait by the door until he returns

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Dog respond physically before he speaks?
According to the passage, what does the Dog say he is waiting for?
Based on the passage, what is the Dog's reply really pointing out about the Traveller?
options: That the Traveller has forgotten his Dog's name
That the Traveller is the one causing the delay, not the Dog
That the Traveller is afraid to travel alone
That the Traveller does not actually want the Dog to come

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Dogs are always more patient than their masters
It is unfair to blame someone else for a delay that is really your own fault
Yawning is a sign of laziness that should be scolded
Travellers should never bring their dogs along

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the Dog stretching himself?
According to the passage, what tone does the Dog use when he answers?
According to the passage, what exact words does the Dog use to describe his own readiness?
As the passage uses it, what does "merely" mean in "the Dog merely wagged his tail"?
Based on the passage, why might the Traveller have assumed the Dog was the one holding things up?
options: He mistook the Dog's stretching and yawning as a sign of reluctance, rather than noticing his own delay
The Dog had refused to go with him the day before
The Dog had actually said he did not want to travel
The Traveller had already packed everything he needed

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Traveller scolds his Dog for being slow, but the Dog calmly points out that he himself is the one causing the delay
A Dog refuses to accompany his master on a journey
A Traveller and his Dog race each other to the door
A Dog falls asleep and misses the start of the journey
